title: How to treat psoriasis with AI and a real dermatologist
summary: Psoriasis treatment online: compare FutureClinic's $40 visit and Honeydew, cash prices, and creams, pills, or biologics a doctor can prescribe by message.
body_markdown:
Plaque psoriasis causes thick, scaly patches on the knees, elbows, lower back, or scalp, and a physician can treat it by message with prescription creams, scalp treatments, pills, or home-injected biologics if your doctor decides it's right for you. In AMN Healthcare's 2025 survey of 15 US metros, new patients waited 36.5 days on average for an in-person dermatologist, and a 2015 study found a medical visit takes 121 minutes on average, travel included.


That wait pushes people online, raising a practical question: do you want another service with all its attached requirements, like multi-month[subscriptions](https://futureclinic.com/blog/telehealth-subscriptions-vs-paying-a-doctor-per-visit-yearly-cost) or custom compounds, or did you just want an expert doctor of your own? If you want what another company sells beyond the doctor, it is a strong option. If you simply wanted a physician, FutureClinic gives you one with nothing attached.


On FutureClinic, you message a state-licensed physician from the web or your AI app and get a reply typically within a few hours, almost always the same day or the next. Every doctor is a physician with an MD, DO or MBBS degree, never a nurse practitioner or physician assistant. No form is approved in bulk: a specific doctor reads your whole case and answers with a Human Signature, a short live video or voice note. Real care takes hours, not seconds. After your first visit, you stay with the same doctor.


## AI psoriasis treatment: why the same doctor matters, and how AI helps


Psoriasis is usually lifelong, with remissions the American Academy of Dermatology (AAD) says most often last 1 to 12 months. Messaging the same doctor time after time builds trust to try treatments together and track progress: checking plaques after four weeks of a steroid, swapping in a vitamin D cream to lower the risk of steroid thinning, or Zoryve or Vtama on skin folds, tapering to prevent a rebound flare, or comparing new labs against last year's for a pill or biologic.


Your doctor's only incentive is to help you. FutureClinic sells no medicines, and your doctor earns nothing extra for any prescription or test, never upselling a medicine or lab panel. With no subscription required, you never stay subscribed monthly to keep your medicine, and your doctor can prescribe any brand or generic to the pharmacy you choose, with no house formulary.


Many people ask ChatGPT or Claude about triggers like strep throat, stress, skin injury, cold weather, lithium, or stopping prednisone. We believe AI is a tool for doctors and the doctor is in charge of every case. Health problems have nuance needing one-to-one attention, and only an expert knows when AI makes a mistake. Behind the scenes, FutureClinic's AI works like a chief resident, gathering your history and photos into a summary you confirm, and never gives medical advice by itself. Connecting your AI app brings your context with you.


The same doctor can help with other problems in their specialty, like eczema, acne, or hair loss. FutureClinic has over 300 doctors. Across more than 60 specialties, you can see primary care doctors and other specialists, and every FutureClinic doctor you see works from one medical record. NIAMS notes psoriasis raises the risk of psoriatic arthritis, heart attacks, strokes, anxiety, and depression.


## What psoriasis treatments can a dermatologist prescribe by message?


Psoriasis affects up to 3.2% of the US population (2019 AAD-NPF guideline). Skin cells multiply in days rather than weeks; 80% to 90% have plaques, and it is not contagious. Fragrance-free creams, salicylic acid, and coal tar help mild scale. After reviewing your history, joint or nail symptoms, pregnancy plans, and three sharp photos in bright natural light against a plain background (one with a coin for scale), your doctor can prescribe creams, scalp treatments, pills, or biologics if your doctor decides it's right for you:


-


**Steroid and vitamin D topicals:** Corticosteroids are the top prescribed treatment, including clobetasol 0.05% cream (up to 2 weeks, ages 12+) and shampoo (up to 4 weeks, adults). To lower the risk of steroid side effects such as thinning skin, the 2021 AAD-NPF guideline advises steroid-sparing agents, alone or alternating with steroids: calcipotriene 0.005% cream, tazarotene cream (contraindicated in pregnancy), or off-label tacrolimus and pimecrolimus for face, folds, and genitals. Calcipotriene-betamethasone ointment combines a vitamin D product with a steroid (ages 12+, up to 4 weeks).


-


**Non-steroidal topicals:** In week 8 trials of once-daily Zoryve (roflumilast 0.3% cream, ages 2+ including folds; 0.3% foam, ages 12+), 41.5% and 36.7% of cream users cleared or almost cleared on average versus 5.8% and 7.1% on vehicle. In week 12 Vtama (tapinarof 1% cream, adults) trials, 36% and 40% were clear or almost clear on average versus 6% on vehicle.


-


**Pills:** Otezla (apremilast 30 mg twice daily after titration) needs no baseline labs; 33.1% and 28.8% reached PASI-75 at week 16 on average versus 5.3% and 5.8% on placebo. Once-daily pills include Sotyktu (deucravacitinib 6 mg; 58% and 53% PASI-75 at week 16 on average versus 13% and 9% on placebo) and Icotyde (icotrokinra 200 mg, approved March 2026 for ages 12+, 40 kg+; 55% PASI-90 at week 16 on average versus 4% on placebo). Methotrexate (contraindicated in pregnancy; both partners stop 3 months before conceiving) and acitretin (avoid pregnancy during and 3 years after) require labs.


-


**Biologics and biosimilars:** A 2025 Cochrane review (204 trials, 67,889 patients) found biologics reached PASI-90 more often on average than non-biologic pills. Home-injected biologics like Skyrizi and biosimilars like adalimumab-fkjp and Otulfi (ustekinumab-aauz) need baseline TB, hepatitis, and blood work at discounted lab prices.


Clinic phototherapy (UVB or excimer laser), cyclosporine (Neoral, needing an exam and blood pressure checks), IV infliximab, and provider-injected Ilumya require in-person care.


## What do visits, medicines, and prior authorizations cost?


A visit is $40 for the best-fit doctor, or a chosen doctor's listed price, typically $20 to $100. Most doctors offer an optional membership (typically $25 to $100 a month) for unlimited care with that doctor, cancel any time. Prescriptions go to the pharmacy you choose, including mail-order pharmacies that deliver to your door, with a discount coupon for the best cash price. As of October 2026, Cost Plus Drugs cash prices before shipping ($5.25 standard; $55 cold-chain) are $7.14 for clobetasol 0.05% cream (30 g), $7.70 for methotrexate 2.5 mg (30 tablets), $423.25 for two adalimumab-fkjp 40 mg pens, and $877.50 for one Otulfi 45 mg syringe; GoodRx coupon prices are $939.86 for Zoryve 0.3% cream (60 g), $1,531.71 for Vtama 1% cream (60 g), $3,353.53 for Otezla (60 tablets), $8,417.84 for Icotyde (30 tablets), and $22,820.90 for one Skyrizi pen.


In a 2019 study, 55.2% of dermatology biologics needed prior authorization, and a 2023 study found 27.2- to 29.7-day average approval waits. When insurance needs a prior authorization, FutureClinic helps get it.
